narrative.summary: On a chilly transatlantic crossing, Neville Fairweather, a controversial businessman, is found stabbed to death. Witnesses claim to have seen him alive on the first-class promenade deck at the time of the murder, but the detective Katherine Bellamy uncovers a cunning impersonation by a crew member disguised as the victim. Through careful deduction and an identity deception mechanism exploiting social logic and class segregation, the true killer, Dr. Cecil Ashgrove, is revealed.

accepted_facts: Neville Fairweather was stabbed to death with a dagger to the heart.
Witnesses saw Neville on the first-class promenade deck around quarter to nine.
A deck steward in a uniform identical to the victim’s was seen mimicking his gestures.
The victim’s cabin doorframe had a torn edge of steward’s uniform fabric.
Crew schedules show the steward’s movements contradict witness sightings of the victim.
Dr. Ashgrove had horological knowledge and access to restricted areas.
The dagger was kept in Dr. Ashgrove’s medical bag in the infirmary.
A glove mark on the dagger belonged to Lavinia Yardley but is explained innocently.
inferred_conclusions: The person seen on the promenade deck was the steward impersonating the victim.
Neville Fairweather was killed earlier in his cabin, not on the promenade deck.
Dr. Ashgrove manipulated witness expectations and crew movements to create a false timeline.
The glove mark misleads suspicion toward Lavinia Yardley, who is innocent.
Dr. Ashgrove's access and skills allowed him to kill and conceal the act.

mechanism.description: The murder was concealed by impersonation: a crew member, Iris Selwyn, disguised in the victim’s usual clothing and mimicking his mannerisms on the first-class promenade deck to create a false impression the victim was alive and present there at the time of the murder. This exploited cognitive bias and social segregation, as passengers expected Neville Fairweather on that deck and did not suspect a steward. Meanwhile, the real victim was stabbed earlier in his cabin. Dr. Ashgrove planned and coordinated the impersonation, using his horological knowledge and access to manipulate crew schedules and alibis.

discriminating_test.design: A staged promenade deck gathering replicates the victim’s distinctive mannerisms and clothing. Witnesses are asked to identify the victim under controlled observation, comparing reactions to the real victim’s known gait and speech versus the steward’s impersonation. The test exposes cognitive bias by revealing that witnesses cannot reliably distinguish the impersonator from the victim, proving the deception.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals that the person seen on the promenade deck at quarter to nine was not Neville Fairweather but Iris Selwyn impersonating him, disproving the false assumption of the victim’s presence and validating the murder time and identity substitution.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Witnesses fail to correctly identify the real victim’s distinctive traits under controlled conditions, confirming identity impersonation.

fair_play.explanation: Step 1: The dagger disturbance in the infirmary and access permissions (early) isolate suspects with access to the weapon. Step 2: Crew schedules and torn uniform fabric (mid) reveal the impersonation, eliminating the victim’s presence on the promenade deck. Step 3: Lavinia Yardley’s glove mark on dagger and confirmed alibi (mid) clear her. Step 4: Dr. Ashgrove’s unique horological knowledge and motive (mid) establish capability. The discriminating test (early act 3) confirms identity deception, enabling the reader to solve the case before the reveal.
